questions.question: What are the two flow directions in Pipecat's pipeline?
options: Input and Output
DOWNSTREAM (source to sink: audio in, TTS out) and UPSTREAM (feedback and control: cancellation, metrics, barge-in)
Forward and Backward
Primary and Secondary
questions.explanation: Pipecat has two flow directions: DOWNSTREAM (source to sink — audio in, through VAD/STT/LLM/TTS, speech out) and UPSTREAM (feedback and control — cancellation frames, metrics, barge-in signals flowing back through the pipeline).

questions.question: What is the typical voice pipeline stage order in Pipecat?
options: LLM -> TTS -> STT -> VAD -> transport
VAD -> STT -> LLM -> TTS -> transport
STT -> VAD -> LLM -> TTS -> transport
transport -> TTS -> LLM -> STT -> VAD
questions.explanation: The canonical Pipecat pipeline runs: VAD (Voice Activity Detection) -> STT (Speech-to-Text) -> LLM -> TTS (Text-to-Speech) -> transport. Each stage is a FrameProcessor that passes Frame objects to the next processor.

questions.question: What are the two LiveKit Agents voice agent classes and when does each apply?
options: SimpleAgent and ComplexAgent; use Simple for easy tasks
MultimodalAgent (direct audio via OpenAI Realtime) and VoicePipelineAgent (STT+LLM+TTS cascade with text-level control)
SpeechAgent and TextAgent; use Speech for voice tasks
FastAgent and SlowAgent; use Fast for low-latency requirements
questions.explanation: LiveKit Agents has two classes: MultimodalAgent (direct audio-in/audio-out via OpenAI Realtime or equivalent — no text in the middle) and VoicePipelineAgent (STT -> LLM -> TTS cascade, giving text-level control at the cost of added latency).

questions.question: What are the 2026 production latency targets for premium voice stacks end-to-end?
options: 1-2 seconds
Under 50ms
questions.explanation: Premium 2026 voice stacks target 450-600ms end-to-end (Vapi ~450-600ms, Retell ~600ms across 180 test calls). Common stacks land at 800-1200ms; anything over 1500ms feels broken to users.

questions.question: What is the 'barge-in' handling requirement in voice agents?
options: The agent must speak louder when background noise is detected
When the user interrupts, an UPSTREAM cancel frame must stop the TTS mid-utterance so the agent does not keep talking over the user
The agent must ask the user to repeat when it cannot hear them
The system must record all user interruptions for later analysis
questions.explanation: Barge-in handling means: when the user interrupts while the agent is speaking, an UPSTREAM cancel frame propagates through Pipecat (or equivalent in LiveKit) to stop the TTS mid-utterance. Without this, the agent keeps talking over the user — a critical UX failure.

questions.question: What is 'semantic turn detection' in voice agents?
options: Using timestamps to detect when the user stops speaking
A transformer model that decides whether the user is truly done speaking based on meaning, not just silence
Detecting when the user says 'over' or 'done'
Analyzing speech volume to detect end of utterance
questions.explanation: Semantic turn detection uses a transformer model to decide whether the user has finished their turn based on semantic understanding, not just silence detection. LiveKit Agents ships this natively.
